memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then put my cup, the silver cup, in the mouth of the youngest one's sack, along with his silver for the grain.' And he did as Joseph said." — Gen 44:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph places his own silver cup in Benjamin's sack. Of all the brothers, Benjamin is chosen — the youngest, the innocent one, the son Jacob loves most. He has done nothing wrong, yet he is the one who will be accused.

This is a deliberate, carefully designed test. Joseph wants to know whether his brothers will sacrifice Benjamin the way they once sacrificed him. Twenty years ago they let their father's favourite son disappear and did not lose any sleep over it. Will they do it again?

It is impossible for a Christian to read this without thinking of another innocent one who carried a charge He did not deserve. Benjamin is only a faint shadow — he is innocent of this particular theft, not sinless. But the pattern is there: the guiltless one bearing the accusation so that the guilty may be exposed and, eventually, restored. At the cross, Jesus took a charge that belonged entirely to us. He was numbered with the transgressors though He had done no wrong (Isa 53:12; 2 Cor 5:21).

Life sometimes places us under accusations we do not deserve. When that happens, we are walking a small stretch of road our Saviour walked first — and He walks it with us still.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you ever been blamed for something you did not do? How did you respond?
2. What does it mean to you that Jesus willingly took a charge that was yours?
3. Is there someone you have been quick to accuse without knowing the full story?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You bore the accusation that belonged to me, and You did it without a word of complaint. Thank You for taking my guilt on Yourself. Help me to be slow to accuse others and quick to trust You when I am wronged. Amen.
